content.title: Arkansas basketball edges Oklahoma, advances to SEC Tournament semifinals
content.text: Updated March 13, 2026, 11:32 p.m. CTNASHVILLE, Tenn. — For the first time since 2022, Arkansas basketball is in the SEC Tournament semifinals. The No. 3 Razorbacks (24-8) capitalized on their double-bye and downed No. 11 Oklahoma 82-79 in the quarterfinals on Friday, March 13. It was the Sooners' third game in as many days, and Arkansas will take on another Cinderella in No. 15 Ole Miss for the right to play in the tournament championship.Florida and Vanderbilt are the other teams alive on the other side of the bracket. The first half was an ugly one for Arkansas. The Hogs shot 41.9% from the field and lost the rebounding battle 22-14. Oklahoma point guard Nijel Pack went off for 16 points, and the Hogs’ supporting cast struggled. Outside of Darius Acuff Jr., no Arkansas player scored more than five points. But Acuff was sensational in his return from a one-game absence. The SEC Player of the Year scored 21 points in the first period and went 4 for 7 on 3-pointers. He drilled a pull-up triple in the final seconds to trim the deficit to two and register his sixth 20-point half of the season. The teams went back-and-forth for the first few minutes of the second period, but Arkansas surged ahead behind a 10-2 spurt. A put-back dunk from Trevon Brazile with 12:37 remaining gave the Hogs a 54-50 lead and forced Oklahoma (19-15) to call a timeout before the under-12. The reset worked, and the Sooners punched back. The teams exchanged scoring runs and the score was tied at 67 with 5:38 remaining when Arkansas went on a decisive 6-0 run. Malique Ewin, Billy Richmond III and Brazile had baskets inside the paint to give Arkansas a 73-67 advantage. A couple possessions later, Acuff drained a pull-up 3-pointer that extended the lead to seven. Oklahoma didn’t go down without a fight and trimmed the lead to two on multiple occasions with fewer than two minutes on the clock, but the Sooners couldn't get over the hump.Acuff made another clutch jumper in the right corner with the shot-clock winding down that meant Arkansas would win if it made its free throws. However, Acuff missed one freebie, and Nijel Pack missed a heave in the final seconds to set Arkansas into the semifinals.Acuff finished with 37 points, five rebounds and five assists. His 37 points are the second-most by a Razorback in the SEC Tournament. Brazile finished with 12 points and 11 rebounds.The Southwest Times Record provided live updates throughout the game. Our recap is below. Watch Arkansas basketball vs Oklahoma in SEC TournamentArkansas basketball vs Oklahoma live score updatesSecond Half Arkansas leads 71-67, 4:25A 4-0 run thanks to a Malique Ewin dunk and a layup from Billy Richmond III forces Oklahoma into another timeout. The Sooners only have one left, and Arkansas is up four in the closing minutes. Darius Acuff Jr. is now up to 31 points, which are the third-most by a Razorback in the SEC Tournament. Oklahoma leads 63-61, 7:46We're headed for a thrilling finish, just like the regular-season meeting between these two teams. Darius Acuff Jr. has 25 points, five rebounds and five assists, but Derrion Reid has come alive for the Sooners in this period and now has 17 points. Paint points, which are usually and advantage for Arkansas, are in Oklahoma's favor by a 36-26 margin. Arkansas leads 54-50, 12:29The Razorbacks are in the midst of a 10-2 run and Oklahoma has to call a timeout before the under-12. Trevon Brazile already has six points and five rebounds in the second period. Oklahoma leads 46-44, 15:40The supporting cast is playing much better through the first 4:20. Meleek Thomas has a 3-pointer, while Trevon Brazile and Nick Pringle have put-back scores. Still, Oklahoma is getting plenty of good shots. One thing to monitor is the foul count. The Sooners have four and the Hogs have zero at the first media timeout.First Half HALF: Oklahoma 39, Arkansas 37Darius Acuff Jr. makes a 3-pointer right before the final buzzer sounds to give him 21 points and trim the deficit to two at the intermission. D.J. Wagner also made a critical triple inside the final minute. At times, this was a very ugly half, but the deficit is still only two points as the Hogs head to the locker room. They need more from Meleek Thomas and Trevon Brazile in the second period. Oklahoma leads 32-27, 3:55This is one of the worst first halves of the season for Arkansas. The Hogs are shooting 36% and losing the rebounding battle 20-10. Trevon Brazile has two fouls and Meleek Thomas is 0 for 4 with two turnovers. Oklahoma is dictating things, but the Sooners only lead by five. Arkansas has to find a way to keep this close entering halftime and then make some adjustments. Oklahoma leads 29-24, 6:27The Sooners have made their last six shots, while Arkansas only has two made field goals from players not named Darius Acuff Jr. The Razorbacks need the supporting cast to step up, but they could also do with some better officiating. The referees have missed two obvious Oklahoma travels and an out-of-bounds call that led to an Sooners' layup. Nigel Pack leads Oklahoma with nine points. Arkansas leads 16-15, 11:15Both teams went into shooting slumps after the first media timeout. Arkansas had a 3:24 scoring drought that ended with free throws from Darius Acuff Jr., who now has 12 points. The Razorbacks need to get some more contributions from the rest of the roster. The highlight of the game so far was a one-handed dunk by Oklahoma's Tae Davis, putting Billy Richmond III on a future poster. Oklahoma leads 11-10, 15:44Darius Acuff Jr. has eight of the Hogs' 10 points, but Oklahoma is generating really good looks of its own at the other end. The teams are a combined 8-for-12 to start the game.Pregame Normal starting lineup returns for ArkansasDarius Acuff Jr. is back and will join Meleek Thomas, Billy Richmond III, Trevon Brazile and Nick Pringle as the Hogs' first five. Tipoff is scheduled for 9:10 p.m.Hello from Nashville. It's been a long day inside Bridgestone Arena. Arkansas and Oklahoma will tipoff at 9:10 p.m. The winner will play Ole Miss tomorrow in the semifinals after the Rebels just pulled off a stunning upset over No. 2 Alabama.What time does Arkansas vs Oklahoma start?Date: Friday, March 13Time: 8:30 p.m. CT Where: Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tenn.What TV channel is Arkansas vs Oklahoma on today? TV Channel: SEC NetworkLivestream: Fubo (free trial), ESPN+How to watch online: Fubo (Free trial), ESPN+ (here's how to stream it live)Arkansas vs Oklahoma predictionThis should be another tight game. Oklahoma has the athleticism and size to give the Hogs problems, but the Sooners don't have an answer for Darius Acuff Jr. The Razorbacks will be the fresher squad and clinch a spot in the SEC Tournament semifinals.
